query: To test whether cue-offset remapping is related to the conflict experienced during combined-cue presentation, analyze both cues across 18 flies. For each fly and each cue, compute cue conflict as the signed circular difference between the both-cues offset and the initial single-cue offset, and compute offset change as the signed circular difference between the final single-cue offset and the initial single-cue offset. Express both values in degrees and wrap them to a circular range such as -180° to 180°, producing two data points per fly. Visualize offset change versus cue conflict as a single scatter plot, with cue conflict on the x-axis and offset change on the y-axis. Show Cue 1 and Cue 2 in the same panel using black and gray points, respectively. Fit the relationship with a circular-noise linear model, such as a Bayesian linear model with von Mises residuals, and overlay the fitted trend line. Save the per-fly per-cue offset values, conflict and change values, cue labels, model fit results, and final figure.

analyse_plan.Objective: Test whether offset remapping is predicted by conflict magnitude.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify Bayesian model specification and MCMC diagnostics; confirm two data points per fly.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the per-fly EPG ΔF/F traces, FicTrac-derived HD time series, visual cue position, wind nozzle position, and block labels for the 18 flies across the protocol's 5 blocks (initial cue 1, initial cue 2, both-cues for 800 s, final cue 1 for 5 min, final cue 2 for 5 min). 2. Preprocess Imaging And Fit Bump: Apply NoRMCorre motion correction, divide PB into 25–40 ROIs, compute per-ROI ΔF/F (10th-percentile baseline), and fit a von Mises per timepoint; discard timepoints with adjusted R² < 0.5 or immobility. 3. Compute Per-Cue Per-Block Offsets: For each fly and for each cue, compute the mean offset (= bump_position − (−cue_position)) during the initial single-cue block, the both-cues block, and the final single-cue block. 4. Compute Conflict And Offset Change Per Cue: For each fly and each cue, define θ_n = both_cue_offset − initial_offset (the cue-conflict measure) and φ_n = final_offset − initial_offset (the offset-change measure); produce two data points per fly, one for cue 1 (less familiar) and one for cue 2 (more familiar). 5. Fit Bayesian Linear Model: Fit the model μ_n = a·θ_n + b, φ_n ~ vonMises(μ_n, κ) using the priors a ~ N(0, 1), b ~ uniform(-π, π), κ ~ inverseGamma(1.91, 6.47) chosen to suppress extreme κ values (with <2% of κ falling below 1 or above 50, validated by prior predictive simulations). 6. Sample Posterior With Stan HMC: Estimate posterior samples for a, b, κ using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo in Stan 2.19.0 via PyStan2 with 4 chains × 1000 samples each after 1000 warm-up samples and no thinning; run HMC diagnostics, examine the pair plots for multimodality, and run posterior retrodictive checks against the data. 7. Save Key Results: Save the per-fly per-cue offsets across the three blocks, the conflict and offset-change values, the posterior samples for a/b/κ, and the Bayesian fit line used for the panel. 8. Visualization: Plot offset change φ_n (final − initial) on the y-axis versus cue conflict θ_n (both − initial) on the x-axis, with two points per fly color-coded by cue (cue 1 in black, cue 2 in gray), and overlay the fit line μ_n = a·θ_n + b from the Bayesian linear model.

key_analysis_results: Offset change predicted by conflict: less familiar cue showed large conflict and large remapping; more familiar cue showed small conflict and small change. Bayesian model provided good fit.
key_analysis_conclusions: Familiar cue instructs remapping of less familiar cue to build self-consistent representation through Hebbian plasticity.

summary_report.abstract: Offset remapping analyzed as function of cue conflict.
summary_report.methods: 18 flies, 36 data points, Bayesian linear model with von Mises noise, Stan HMC (4 chains x 1000 samples).
summary_report.results: Linear relationship; cue 1 (less familiar) shows large remapping, cue 2 shows little.
summary_report.discussion: Direct evidence for familiarity-guided spatial learning.
